newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-ANALYSIS OF GRAF V COETZER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-ANALYSIS OF GRAF V COETZER.

text.p: Analysis of Tuesday's French Open women's singles quarter-final between second seed Steffi Graf of Germany and 11th seed Amanda Coetzer of South Africa, won 6-1 6-4 by Coetzer.

Graf, making unusual unforced errors, lost her first two serves and went 4-0 down after just 18 minutes. She saved two break points in the fifth game before eventually winning her serve. But Coetzer won the next game and then broke Graf again with the German hitting a backhand long on set point.
Coetzer broke Graf to go 2-0 up. The reigning champion broke back, only to lose her serve again in the fourth game and allow Coetzer to lead 3-1. Rain then interrupted play for some 30 minutes.

After the break, Graf seemed a little more aggressive and made fewer mistakes. Both players held serve until the 10th game, which lasted over 15 minutes. Graf wasted several opportunities to win her serve before hitting a forehand long to give Coetzer a match point. The South African converted it thanks to another unforced error by Graf to win after one hour and 32 minutes of a one-sided contest.
